recentKeyChanges.title: Q2 earnings: record $28.2B revenue, but op margin collapses to 1.4% and FCF goes negative
recentKeyChanges.description: Tesla reported Q2 2026 financials on July 22 after the already-known 480,126 delivery / 451,758 production print. Revenue hit a record $28.236B (+26% YoY, beat ~$26.4–27.6B Street), and TTM revenue crossed $100B for the first time. The P&L underneath is ugly: non-GAAP EPS $0.33 vs ~$0.53 expected (miss of ~$0.20), operating income $398M (−57% YoY), operating margin 1.4% (vs 4.1% YoY and vs ~5.4% pre-earnings Street consensus), free cash flow −$1.092B on CapEx of $5.789B (+142% YoY). Gross margin held relatively better at 16.8% (−41 bps YoY), so the damage was opex and mix, not just discounting. Regulatory credit revenue collapsed to $146M (−67% YoY from $439M), removing near-pure profit after the federal EV credit / CAFE penalty market evaporated. GAAP net income $1.114B (−5% YoY) was propped by ~$590M other income (bitcoin MTM / FX). Management framed CapEx run-rate above $25B for full-year 2026 as deliberate AI/robotics/autonomy spend. Market verdict: TSLA fell ~14.5% on July 23 to ~$320, erasing >$140B market value — one of the steeper single-day drops in years. Critical read: the Q2 delivery beat did not translate into a healthy auto quarter. Volume was inventory-fed (prod 28k below del), ASP pressure + AI opex + dead credit line crushed operating leverage. Cash burn better than the −$3.25B Street worst-case, but 1.4% op margin is incompatible with a re-rating of the car business.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Headlines split 'revenue beat / EPS miss'; reality is a structural profit collapse (1.4% op margin, negative FCF, credits gone) that the stock priced with a ~14.5% one-day drop.

recentKeyChanges.title: TSLA drops ~14.5% post-earnings as Street digests profit miss and $25B+ CapEx path
recentKeyChanges.description: On July 23, the first full session after the Q2 report, Tesla shares fell approximately 14.5%, closing near $320 after opening around $374, wiping out more than $140B in market value on heavy volume. The move ranks among Tesla's steeper single-day percentage declines in years. The catalyst was not the already-known delivery beat but the combination of a large EPS miss ($0.33 vs ~$0.53), 1.4% operating margin, negative free cash flow, and management's willingness to run CapEx above $25B for 2026 with limited new concrete Robotaxi/Optimus commercial milestones on the call. Pre-earnings IR consensus had already baked in thin margins and negative FCF; the actual 1.4% op margin undershot even that cautious setup. Critical read: the market is no longer willing to re-rate the auto business on volume alone while AI/robotics spend suppresses near-term profitability. Delivery strength is being treated as a one-quarter inventory/demand bounce, not proof of durable high-margin auto growth.
